answer.origin: Motley Fool opinion article by Keithen Drury, published 2026-07-06. It relays an unnamed average analyst EPS consensus for FY2028 and management commentary from an earlier Nvidia quarterly call whose date is not given.
answer.note: Material claim: as relayed in a 2026-07-06 Motley Fool opinion piece, the average analyst projects FY2028 (ending January 2028) EPS of $12.76, which the author calls conservative. The article also attributes to Nvidia management an expectation that hyperscaler spending will top $1 trillion in 2027 after a projected $650 billion in 2026, and says Wall Street expects 82% growth for the rest of the current year and 41% for 2027, with the metric not specified. Conditionally, this supports a view that Nvidia's forward earnings expectations are high and that hyperscaler capital spending is the demand driver management cites. The EPS figure is a secondary relay of an unnamed consensus, not a verified company result or a dated consensus snapshot. The hyperscaler figures are a management forecast of uncertain date. The author's $319 price estimate at a 25x multiple and his upside view are his own derivations from that EPS, not independent evidence.
limitations: The consensus source, number of contributing analysts, and date of the $12.76 FY2028 EPS average are not disclosed.
It is not stated whether the $12.76 EPS figure is GAAP or non-GAAP.
The quarterly call in which management forecast $650 billion (2026) and over $1 trillion (2027) hyperscaler spending is not identified, and the article gives no statement date for that forecast.
The 82% and 41% growth figures do not specify the metric (revenue, EPS, or other), so they cannot be treated as Nvidia revenue or earnings growth without confirmation.
The article's publication date of 2026-07-06 is not a statement date for the analyst consensus or the management forecast.
follow_up: Check a dated consensus source for Nvidia FY2028 EPS to confirm the $12.76 average, its contributor count, its date, and whether it is GAAP or non-GAAP.

Check the Nvidia quarterly earnings transcript and release for the statement that hyperscaler spending will top $1 trillion in 2027 after $650 billion in 2026, recording the call date and the exact wording of the forecast.
Check whether the 82% (rest of current year) and 41% (2027) analyst growth figures refer to revenue or EPS, and compare them with the consensus dataset for the same period.
